issues.description: The Person model in the solution repository uses a different attribute name for the first name ('givenName' with getGivenName/setGivenName) while the problem statement and the template repository define and expect 'firstName' (getFirstName/setFirstName). Other solution code (e.g. PersonService and client views/controllers) still reference getFirstName/setFirstName, creating a structural mismatch that will prevent compilation and confuse students about the correct model fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the field and accessor methods back to 'firstName' (getFirstName/setFirstName) in src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java, or update all usages in server and client code to use 'givenName' consistently. Prefer restoring 'firstName' to match the problem statement and the template to avoid breaking the intended exercises.

issues.description: The Person model's first name field is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement (and the template code) refer to the attribute as 'firstName' (with corresponding getFirstName/setFirstName), while the solution's common Person class uses 'givenName' (getGivenName/setGivenName). This breaks the conceptual mapping for students (the UML and client code expect firstName) and creates confusion when comparing the template/problem with the provided solution and other code that still references firstName.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's Person attribute and accessors from 'givenName'/'getGivenName'/'setGivenName' to 'firstName'/'getFirstName'/'setFirstName' so the solution matches the problem statement, template model, and other code references (and update any usages in service/controller code accordingly).
